title: Auditflow SIEM adapter requirements and integration notes
content:
Purpose:
This note collects design constraints and a customer-facing checklist for the new ‘Auditflow’ SIEM export adapter prototype (Splunk / Datadog / Sentinel). Aim: create a small-footprint connector that can be deployed by customers or run as a managed forwarder with clear RBAC boundaries and evidence automation hooks.

Scope & goals:
- Support via native collectors and HTTP ingestion for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, and Azure Monitor (Sentinel) HTTP Data Collector. No heavy forwarder dependency required.
- Preserve audit fidelity: 1:1 event ordering where possible, monotonic request_id, and minimal mutation of original event fields.
- Support per-tenant data residency and field-level redaction (PII).
- Provide integration guidance and a simple checklist for onboarding SOC teams.

Event format and mapping notes:
- Transport: JSON newline-delimited preferred. For customers needing CEF/GELF, provide mapping adapters with loss warnings.
- Core audit schema (recommended canonical names):
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - tenant_id
  - workspace_id
  - request_id (idempotency key)
  - actor_id / actor_type
  - action (namespace:operation e.g., auth:token.create)
  - resource_type / resource_id
  - result (success|failure|partial)
  - outcome_code (numeric, internal)
  - src_ip / user_agent
  - service_context (map of tags: route/model/region)
  - evidence_id (if evidence bundle attached)
  - raw_payload (optional compressed base64 for deep inspection)

- Field guidance: prefer flat keys; nested maps allowed under service_context. Keep event size < 512KB; chunk payloads for large evidence links rather than embedding.

RBAC v2 considerations (customer-facing):
- Export tokens must be tied to an export role (exporter.read, exporter.manage, audit.admin).
- Managed forwarder should be able to request short-lived tokens via customer-managed OIDC to avoid long-lived secrets in infra.
- Cross-tenant export denied by default. Admins can grant workspace-level export scopes.

Evidence automation hooks (design):
- Evidence bundles: separate object store (S3/GCS/Azure) with signed, time-limited URLs. Events include evidence_id and evidence_manifest_url; SIEM teams can fetch raw artifacts when needed.
- Retention markers: include retention_policy and legal_hold flags in events to drive downstream retention and e-discovery.
- Proof-of-export: connector should emit an export_ack event (export_ack_type: delivered|retry|dropped) with md5/sha256 checksums for forensics.

Connector operational requirements:
- Throughput: baseline 2k events/sec per connector instance; should autoscale horizontally.
- Batching: default 100 events per batch or 1s flush. Backpressure: exponential backoff with jitter (max 5 retries) and persistent queue to disk up to 10GB.
- Ordering: best-effort ordering; provide per-tenant sequence numbers to assist SIEM dedupe.
- Idempotency: include request_id and sequence_number. Consumers should use request_id as dedupe key.
- Metrics & alerting: exporter must emit exporter.metrics for: queue_depth, send_latency, last_success_ts, last_failure_reason, retry_count. Expose OpenTelemetry metrics endpoint.

Splunk specifics:
- Preferred: HEC endpoint with token-based auth. HEC batch size limits and max event size documented in Splunk spec; connector must split oversized events and emit meta events when split occurs.
- CEF support via optional transformation layer; note that some audit fields may not have direct CEF mapping (evidence_id should be sent as 'extension' field).

Datadog specifics:
- Use Logs intake API; recommend API keys or API key + app key with scoped roles. Support log rehydration via Log Pipelines tags (service: redwood-audit).

Azure Sentinel specifics:
- Use Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector API; recommend customer provide a workspace key scoped to ingest only. For customers using Azure Sentinel connectors, include guidance for mapping evidence_id to Microsoft.MessageId or customProperties.

Customer onboarding checklist (quick):
- Confirm destination (Splunk HEC / Datadog Logs / Azure Monitor) and regional endpoint.
- Confirm retention & residency constraints; provide evidence store location if required.
- Decide on token model: long-lived token vs OIDC short-lived. Recommend OIDC for enterprise.
- Provide sample dataset (100–500 events) with representative PII and large-evidence cases for test ingestion.
- Confirm alerting & SLO: desired delivery SLA, acceptable loss policy (drop|retry|archive).
- Contractual items: encryption in transit, KMS integration for keys, breach notification timelines.

Operational runbook snippets (to include in final doc):
- On exporter queue growth: check destination quotas -> rotate tokens -> scale connector -> open incident if >15 minutes backlog.
- On repeated 4xx errors from destination: verify token scopes and IP allowlists; escalate to customer to add connector IP range.

Privacy & redaction patterns:
- Redaction levels: none | structured-redact | remove-field | tokenise (replace with hash).
- Provide declarative redaction config per-tenant: include allow-list of fields to keep, and blacklist regex patterns.

Security & cryptographic considerations:
- Sign export_ack with connector private key for proof-of-export. Keep key in HSM for managed instances; recommend customer KMS for private deployments.
- Fields that are sensitive (ssn, cc, full_text of user messages) should be redacted before export unless explicitly allowed.

Limitations & open questions (work-in-progress):
- How to represent multi-part evidence bundles in SIEM that only accept flat fields? Current plan: emit manifest URL and small manifest JSON; SIEM enrichment pipelines can fetch externally if allowed.
- Deduplication semantics vary by SIEM; need to publish per-SIEM best-effort dedupe guide.
- Should we provide a hosted forwarder vs. OSS connector? Cost/ops tradeoffs to discuss with GTM.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Marco: prototype HEC batching split logic (P0) — RFC due 2025-03-10.
- Alex: write example transformation scripts for CEF/GELF (P1).
- Priya: draft customer onboarding template & SOC runbook (this doc -> v0.1) and coordinate legal redaction policy.

Appendix A: sample JSON event (newline-delimited)
{
  "timestamp": "2025-03-01T21:07:13.512Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "workspace_id": "ws-prod-us-1",
  "request_id": "req_8a7f0b9e",
  "actor_id": "user:alice@example.com",
  "actor_type": "human",
  "action": "auth:token.revoke",
  "resource_type": "key",
  "resource_id": "key-12",
  "result": "success",
  "src_ip": "198.51.100.14",
  "service_context": {"route": "/v1/generate", "model": "rwlm-3b"},
  "evidence_id": "ev_20250301_001",
  "evidence_manifest_url": "https://s3.region.amazonaws.com/rdw-evidence/ev_20250301_001/manifest.json"
}

Feedback welcome — flag anything that will block SOC ingestion or legal review.
